clue.text: Passed on zip that doesn't work

parts.note: someone who has passed on has died, so is dead
zip is slang for nothing, and a duck is a score of nothing in cricket

explanation.surface: Someone who has died leaves behind a broken zip fastener.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a batter's score of zero in cricket, so it stands for 'zip', meaning nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead duck is an idea or plan doomed to failure, something useless that will never succeed.

clue.text: Drink Roy's opening is revolutionary, having no ring pull

parts.note: cha is an informal word for tea, a drink

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, so this takes the start of Roy's

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: having no ring tells us to remove a ring-shaped letter from the revolutionary's name

parts.note: Mao Zedong was the Chinese communist revolutionary
the letter O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A drink can is opened by spinning it, since its ring pull is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring pull' looks like one thing, a can's tab; 'ring' belongs to the wordplay and 'pull' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Charisma is personal magnetism, the attractive power a person has over others, which is a kind of pull.

clue.text: Panic-stricken quartet gatecrashing ?

indicators.note: a gatecrasher pushes into an event uninvited, so the quartet's letters push into the other piece

parts.note: the printed question mark stands for a query
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Four musicians in a panic barge into a gathering, and the clue ends with a puzzled question mark.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark stands apart with a space before it: it is not punctuation but a piece of the wordplay, a query.
explanation.definitionFit: Quivery means trembling or shaking, which is how someone gripped by panic behaves.

clue.text: Perform the role of right-winger, number 26?

parts.note: to perform the role of something is to be a one
Con is short for Conservative, a right-winger in UK politics

explanation.surface: An actor asks to play a right-wing character listed as number 26.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'be a con', to act as a Conservative. 26 across is PHAROS, the lighthouse of Alexandria; the question mark marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A lighthouse is a signal light guiding ships, a classic beacon, and the Pharos was the most famous.

clue.text: Set menu item in Mexico with / without wine

indicators.note: without the wine means those letters are taken out of the dish

parts.note: a burrito is a Mexican tortilla wrap
It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and it
w/ is a written shorthand for with

explanation.surface: A set menu offers a Mexican dish, with or without wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with / without' reads as the menu's 'with or without'; the slash belongs to 'with', since w/ is shorthand for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A badger's home is called a set, and a burrow is likewise an animal's dug-out home.

clue.text: Club's goals recalled by United international, having cracked domestic title

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word for goals is read backwards

parts.note: in football the net is the goal
house as an adjective means domestic, as in house rules

indicators.note: having cracked means these letters broke into the title

parts.note: Mr is a title
U is the abbreviation for United in team names

explanation.surface: A football club's goals are remembered by a Manchester United international who has won the domestic league title.
explanation.walkthrough: Stenhousemuir is a Scottish football club, so the 's is a link ('is').
explanation.definitionFit: Stenhousemuir FC is a Scottish professional football club based near Falkirk.

clue.text: Standing over drunken Ada, Don's put the lid on booze

indicators.note: in a down answer, standing over means sitting on top of the following letters

parts.note: to scotch something is to put an end to it, putting the lid on it

indicators.note: drunken suggests the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Don stands over a drunk woman named Ada and confiscates the alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don's' is part of the anagram fodder, apostrophe and all, so ADA DONS gives AND SODA, with SCOTCH placed above it.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotch and soda is a whisky mixed with soda water, an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Store with Barker and Jason centrally in picture

parts.note: a reservoir is a store of water or anything held in reserve
a dog is an animal that barks

indicators.note: centrally means the middle letter of Jason is taken

explanation.surface: A shop features two actors, a Barker and a Jason, in its photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: Barker and Jason look like names of people; Barker is a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Reservoir Dogs is a 1992 Quentin Tarantino film, and picture is a common word for a film.

clue.text: Present rebuffed by the European, Stevie?

indicators.note: rebuffed means pushed back, so the word for present runs backwards

parts.note: the present is now
der is the German word for the

explanation.surface: A gift is turned down by a European man called Stevie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift but means now, at this time.
explanation.definitionFit: Stevie Wonder is the famous American singer, so his surname fits 'Stevie' with the question mark marking it.

clue.text: Boundary stroke Lord's devotee wanted

parts.note: a six is a boundary hit in cricket, VI in Roman numerals
to stroke is to caress

explanation.surface: A cricketer hits a boundary shot, and a fan of Lord's cricket ground is wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is London's famous cricket ground, but here the Lord is God. 'wanted' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicaress is a female vicar or vicar's wife, a churchwoman devoted to serving God.

clue.text: Cockney reportedly roused more anger

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker drops the H, and reportedly means we go by how the word is heard

parts.note: roused more, stirred up further, is higher; with the Cockney's dropped aitch that becomes 'igher

explanation.surface: A Londoner is said to have stirred up even more fury.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney means the H is dropped: 'igher sounds like IRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ire is a literary word for anger or wrath.

clue.text: Councillor entering reserves work clothing

indicators.note: entering means the councillor goes inside the reserves

parts.note: subs, substitutes, are the reserves in a team

explanation.surface: A local councillor joins the reserve players wearing work clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrubs are the loose hygienic garments worn by surgeons and nurses at work.

clue.text: Pen industry latterly knocked out by mass disease

parts.note: to pen something is to ring or enclose it

indicators.note: latterly knocked out means the final letter is removed

parts.note: industry means hard work
m is the symbol for mass in physics

explanation.surface: Pen-making industry has recently been wiped out by a widespread disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'latterly knocked out' cuts the K from WORK.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringworm is a contagious fungal infection of the skin, a disease despite its name.

clue.text: Swimmer wearing armbands gulps

indicators.note: gulps means swallows, so the answer is swallowed inside these words

explanation.surface: A child swimmer in armbands swallows water.
explanation.definitionFit: A gar is a long-snouted fish, and fish are swimmers.

clue.text: Bird labourer notes from behind

parts.note: a jack is a labourer or manual worker, as in jack of all trades

indicators.note: from behind means the word is read from its end

parts.note: a wad is a bundle of banknotes

explanation.surface: A worker records birdsong notes while hidden behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: The jackdaw is a small grey-naped crow, a common British bird.

clue.text: Con, given time, that's associated with Morse

parts.note: to do someone is to con or cheat them

explanation.surface: A convict given a prison sentence has links to Inspector Morse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Con, given time' paints a prisoner; Morse is the code, not the detective.
explanation.definitionFit: Morse code is made of dots and dashes, so a dot is part of Morse.

clue.text: Member divided just over three pounds, maybe for barman

indicators.note: divided means the word is cut in half, and the second half is used

parts.note: fifty-one ounces, LI in Roman numerals plus oz, is just over three pounds (forty-eight ounces)

explanation.surface: A club member is split over spending just over three pounds, maybe for the bartender.
explanation.walkthrough: A barman is not a bartender here but someone who fills bars of music. 'maybe for' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Hector Berlioz was a French composer, and composers write music in bars.

clue.text: Scotsman dons tie? Same perhaps

indicators.note: dons means puts on, so the Scotsman wears the tie around it

parts.note: Euan is a Scottish man's name
to rope is to tie

explanation.surface: A Scotsman puts on a tie, wondering whether it's the same one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Same' is not 'identical' but a Sámi, one of the Lapp people of northern Scandinavia.
explanation.definitionFit: A Same, or Sámi, lives in Lapland across Norway, Sweden and Finland, so is an example of a European.

clue.text: Inert character Garth shuffled into line

indicators.note: into means the shuffled letters are put inside the line

parts.note: a ley is a line, as in ley lines

indicators.note: shuffled means Garth's letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A sluggish man named Garth is shuffled into a queue.
explanation.walkthrough: A ley is a line in the sense of ley lines, the supposed alignments of ancient sites.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethargy is sluggishness, an inert state or character lacking energy.

clue.text: Flipping homework left on old floor

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so the word for homework is read backwards

parts.note: prep is school homework, short for preparation
ex means former or old

explanation.surface: Annoyed homework is left lying on an old floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild British curse but signals the reversal. 'floor' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To floor someone is to baffle or stump them completely.

clue.text: Garden rubbish — right tip belonging to some sloth?

parts.note: Eden is the biblical garden
tat is cheap rubbish

indicators.note: the right tip of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Garden rubbish is tipped right, and some of it belongs to a sluggish person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sloth' looks like laziness but is the animal; the question mark marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Edentates are toothless mammals such as sloths, anteaters and armadillos.

clue.text: Spruce up north grazed?

parts.note: grazed means eaten, as cattle graze on grass

explanation.surface: The north looks tidier after being grazed by livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: To neaten is to tidy, and spruce up means to make neat.

clue.text: Become old and broadcast bucket list?

parts.note: to age is to become old

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: Grow old and tell everyone about the things you want to do before you die.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is a list of things to be done, and a bucket list is a list of things to do before you die.

clue.text: Slow down Liverpool fan crossing pitch

indicators.note: crossing means the fan goes across the pitch, around it

parts.note: Liverpool FC play in red, so a fan is a Red
pitch and tar are both black sticky substances

explanation.surface: A Liverpool supporter is slowed down when running across the football field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' looks like a football field but is the sticky black substance.
explanation.definitionFit: To retard is to delay or hold back progress, making something slower.

clue.text: Jumper stocked by retro outfitter

indicators.note: stocked by means the answer is held within these words

explanation.surface: A vintage clothes shop sells a woollen pullover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' looks like a British sweater but is an animal that jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: Roo is short for kangaroo, an animal that moves by jumping.

clue.text: Bandage plugging open wound causes calmness

indicators.note: plugging means the bandage fills a gap in the other letters
wound, as in twisted round, means the letters are rearranged

parts.note: to tape a wound is to bandage it

explanation.surface: A dressing stops an open wound, which brings a patient calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' looks like an injury but is the past tense of wind, turning NOEP from 'open'.
explanation.definitionFit: Not a peep means total silence, no sound at all, a kind of quiet calm.

clue.text: Boozer, typically with artist, knocked back 8

parts.note: PH is short for public house, a boozer

indicators.note: knocked back means the letters are turned round

parts.note: so can mean in this way, typically
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A drinker, as usual with an artist, downs a drink at number 8.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' looks like drinking but reverses SORA. 8 refers to 8 across, a WONDER.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pharos of Alexandria, a lighthouse, was one of the Seven Wonders of the ancient world.

clue.text: Highlands resident cooked bangers and legumes occasionally

indicators.note: cooked means prepared, so the letters are reworked
occasionally means every other letter of legumes is taken

explanation.surface: Someone from the Scottish Highlands prepared sausages with beans.
explanation.walkthrough: Bangers are British slang for sausages. 'occasionally' takes EUE from legumes for the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aberdeen Angus is a Scottish breed of beef cattle, and Aberdeen lies in the north-east Highlands region.
